I've been having this exact issue since the big update, I thought I needed a new GPU! Quest 2 & 3, 5800X3D+6900XT. However, it happens regardless of whether the menus are open or not. But, it's just like you said, happens only in VRChat and the severity depends on the world. For me, I've been doing my testing in the VR Dancing world. The frame skipping/jittering is guaranteed to happen when on the dance floor. Using Air Link or Virtual Desktop doesn't make a difference, H.264 or HEVC encoding doesn't either, and it still happens even on a Quest 3 so the headset isn't the culprit. From my observation in testing, the issue can be amplified when using anti-aliasing and/or higher resolution than native, increasing frame timings. So for the time being I keep my resolution at 100% (~2kx2k) and set anti-aliasing to off in the VRChat graphics settings menu to minimize it as much as I can until there is a fix.

Quick update 12-8-2023: Just got a Radeon 7900XT to see if it would solve my issue. Unfortunately not. Another friend I have who has the same card and CPU as mine doesn't have this issue so it's likely not a hardware issue. I also just discovered the same issue also happens in Half-Life: Alyx in addition to major frame drops. At this point I feel like I need an entirely new computer.

Update 12-12-2023: A day or two after my last update, the issue was resolved! I'm not sure how other than maybe a fresh GPU driver install was what did it? I used DDU (Display Driver Uninstall) when installing the new GPU and when I reverted back to the 6900XT. Even with Virtual Desktop and anti-aliasing enabled having the big menu open, there was no frame jitter! Fingers crossed it stays fixed.🤞

@{6055b9933ae6ab2b062ae057|full_name}: As of 12-12-23 this issue seems to be fixed for me, is it the same story for you? I did a clean install of the latest Adrenaline drivers after using DDU if you want to replicate my process, but also re-seat your GPU before all that, who knows maybe that had an effect.

Edit 12-16-23: Nevermind my original comment, it still jitters, but I have found out that restarting VRChat relieves it somewhat.

@{5ebc41d83ce28333f939867e|full_name}: nope, still broken.

been using DDU for every driver update since AMD is so unreliable when it comes to new driver updates.

same issue.

I've made progress diagnosing the source of this issue! The culprit appears to be the HMD itself as the jittering occurs even while in the standalone Quest home environment which explains why even on a completely newly-built PC the jittering is still present. I've observed this on the Quest 2, 3, and Pro. My hunch as to why it seemed as though the PC contributed to it is because certain applications or worlds affect the frame rate and frame timing being sent to the headset and the two devices are not in sync with one another, like not having Freesync/G-Sync to smooth out the motion of the image. The lower the FPS or greater the frame times, the more likely the jittering occurs. I created a video documenting my findings and shared it with Meta support. Hopefully they fix this via a software update.

https://youtu.be/3thL6tr646E?si=jKXuxC2JNxQd9PGO

details:
Since the newest update, ive noticed a MASSIVE frame time issue when opening the UI.

I have attached 2 Videos, (one with Virtual Desktop Debug and the other with SteamVR Debug), and Virtual Desktop is JUST fine, however, when looking at the SteamVR debug, it shows frame times going red like CRAZY. 

If you look closely in the videos, you can even see it stutter and chop.

Video #1 https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/775275020268077069/1167719413550698547/7df3d669421073a825b28aac692c4130.mp4?ex=654f2673&is=653cb173&hm=ec3f292c931c975c621f9629f4afe72799f230d66c0b899d760e709ffe202af4&

Video #2 https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/775275020268077069/1167718961295671366/4e8fdd63e28246d85604de920a3e2c98.mp4?ex=654f2607&is=653cb107&hm=be201c782842c355eaaa8b069b38eb15e47341c7ac6a439b1181b5fa61aa9d90&

Currently, as of making this post, we have updated GPU Drivers (6900xt with LIGHT OC), Windows Updated to latest, all VRC setting are EXCATLY the same from the last update, except for turning OFF Anti-Aliasing (cause I thought for SOME reason, that was the issue), x570 Mobo with JUST updated BIOS to 4601. *and if it REALLY helps, im using the "--disable-hw-video-decoding" parameter when launching the game.

I honestly CANT think of anything else to report. cause all other games like, Beat Saber, HLA, Pavlov. All run JUST FINE, and without the Frame Timing issue!

Beat Saber is a easy to run game, and even with cranked settings its just fine, HLA is a little more intense, and I only saw issues when loading (cause HLA is on our HDD, not our SSD), and Pavlov, is. well, fine.

I hope others have this issue, cause if its just me, I know the devs prob will skip over this and never fix it.
title: Frame Times go WILD when Menu UI is open
